utterances.text: D7 will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D8, Article 240 of the same constitution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: D8 will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D9, Article 281, paragraphs 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: D9 will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D10, Article 327 of the constitution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I indicate that there's a problem there, because the document I was handed did not include 327. It in fact commenced in the B/C/S with Article -- it was 327, but the English translation commenced at Article 334. There seems to have been a misstapling of the wrong documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for the mistake. It is our mistake, and we will rectify it as soon as possible. If only B/C/S version may be received, and we shall submit its English translation on Monday. Once again, we apologise for the mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That was Article 327, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that will be D10.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D11, decision by the presidency of the SFRY, dated 18 October 1991. The original is in English, and its translation is into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: D11 is received. Now, there was another matter you wished to raise, was there, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, and thank you for the opportunity to raise it. Firstly, I would kindly ask if there is an opportunity in the course of the next week to find some time for some words that we would like to deliver orally with regard to the submission that was handed to you by the OTP on the 24th December. This is Prosecution's motion [In English] 15 December concerning the time for submission of expert reports. [Interpretation] As far as I understand, your decision is still pending on this motion. I would kindly ask for 10 or 15 minutes. The Defence would like to present some arguments with regard to the request that has been made, and our position in that respect may be different, in view of some of the conversations that we have had with our learned friends from the OTP. That is the first issue that I would like to raise. The second issue that I would like to raise is the following: It has to do with the health condition of my client. After the decision that you made immediately prior to our session in December, the Defence, bearing in mind your recommendation contained in that decision, the Defence requested from the Registry to provide some medical examinations which are of the importance for the health condition of our client and which would have a bearing on the way our client is able to follow this procedure. We have received approval by the secretariat for our doctor to be appointed and to have an opportunity to examine our client. We submitted this request immediately after having received the decision by the Registry. We received this decision three days ago. And within the shortest possible time, we would like to make the most of this opportunity. What this is all about: The analysis of what we deem to be important, in view of the overall medical condition of our client, it is necessary for a detailed medical examination and testing of our client to be carried out in the Detention Unit. For that purpose, the expert whom we have engaged, in keeping with the usual practice that is applied in the medical field, it is necessary for the client to be available for two consecutive days, for five to seven hours every day. Our medical expert should arrive on Tuesday or on Wednesday. He is actually arriving on Monday, and the testing should take place on Tuesday and on Wednesday. Given the time frame that is necessary for all the testing and examinations, since the testing has to be done correctly, in keeping with the rules of the medical practice, the Defence counsel kindly request the Trial Chamber to adjourn on Tuesday and on Wednesday, in order to enable our medical experts to carry out all the necessary medical testings of our client, in keeping with the rules of the medical profession. This will enable us to receive the results, which will not be distorted by any of the circumstances that may come into play, such as tiredness and other factors. So I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to make a ruling not to sit on Tuesday and Wednesday in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is in the coming week, you propose, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honour, this is the first that we have been told of this, and I must express vehemently my objection to not being told that there was such a consideration, given the very open, transparent nature of the discussion about ordering of witnesses, inconvenience to witnesses, and the need to have the trial move on. I have seen Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Rodic daily this past week, and I was here all of last week, and this is again, I think, perhaps a matter that reflects a need for an improvement of relations and communication from the Defence to the Prosecution. Secondly, a day has 24 hours, 20 approximately of which my staff is working, and I understand that it may be difficult to arrange around the day, but this Chamber does not hold an eight-hour session, and I would strongly advocate that if the expert has been brought here without consultation with the Chamber, that the responsibility for arranging hours is at the Defence's -- is in the Defence's court, as it were, and that it should have no bearing upon the orderly progression of this trial. Again, all things, I think, can be discussed frankly and openly, and I'm very surprised and disappointed that that is dropped on all of us, with the resulting potential mess that it can have, and the unfairness, potentially, to the client. Again, Defence counsel have to drive their own train on this issue, but it can't be done unilaterally, even if invited by the Court to do so in its order. Accordingly, I would ask that there be no deferral or other delay in order to achieve this, but rather, weekends are also available if need be, and after court session, or if it's an afternoon session, then the morning. But again, this is a matter that has to be arranged so that all parties have notice and that all interests are represented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you will allow me, Your Honour. I appreciate some of what my friend has said. However, we only learned this the way we did, and as soon as we learned that this would take place, we informed the Trial Chamber. When we were in the position to find out when this could be organised, we informed you. We could have done it earlier today, that is true, but we didn't. We know what conditions in the Detention Unit are, and I have to remind you that this is impossible to be done on weekends. At least so far it hasn't been possible. There may have been exceptions, but, as a rule, this is impossible. I believe I am right. If I'm not, I believe that the registrar will correct me. As far as the schedule of the witnesses is concerned, which -- and something that the Prosecution says was our unilateral move, there were such changes without any influence on our part. The Trial Chamber has pointed to that fact, and the Trial Chamber told us that such changes are something that is not in keeping with the usual procedure. I understand that this may cause some problems, but believe me, the problems that the accused is facing are enormous, and I believe that they are even bigger than the problems that any of the witnesses may be experiencing by having to stay a day longer in The Hague waiting to be brought before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are conscious that there are already reasons why witnesses such as Mr. Brolund have to be away from The Hague by fixed times next week. For that reason, we are disinclined to interfere with the present programme during the coming week. I think that must mean, Mr. Petrovic, that your client will be able to be examined each morning, from Monday to Thursday of this coming week, when we are not listed to be hearing the matter. If there was a particular reason why a particular test or examination might take a little longer, we could entertain a detailed submission for us to commence sitting a little later on one day. But if the medical examinations that are thought necessary by the Defence can be got under way, it would seem probable that they can be accommodated over the mornings that are available during the coming week. So, for the moment, we will not change the listing programme, and we will -- if there is a particular difficulty, I have indicated there may be a capacity, on Wednesday or Thursday, in particular, to look at a slightly later start, if that will assist. And we must leave it to you to bring forward that detailed proposal, if there's a need for it, and to justify it. We are conscious in taking this view that there are quite a number of hours in the day, and with the mornings available, as they are next week, it would seem that it ought to be possible for proper and adequate examinations to be undertaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, I've indicated Monday to Thursday. We are told that it would be feasible for us to sit on Friday, in the morning rather than the afternoon, and we are proposing to do that at the present time. But that would leave you from Monday through until Thursday able to give effect to examinations in the morning, and we would hope that it will be possible to achieve all that is necessary in that time. We will adjourn now until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of January 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.56 p.m.
